notes: Two copilot lifetimes over ONE session: turn 1 → clean /exit → relaunch with --resume=<same id> → turn 2. The scenario's whole point is that the SECOND lifetime lands on the SAME session row, so every phase after the birth is pinned with same_session_as: v1_turn_start — if copilot forked into a new session directory, v2_session_resume/v2_pid_rebind/v2_turn_start cannot match and the cell fails loudly. The first birth is UNPINNED (no same_session_as) for the reason the sibling session-end cell records: copilot creates its session directory at launch but events.jsonl only at the first prompt, so a proc-<PID> pre-session may or may not be sampled, and when events.jsonl appears it already holds session.start … user.message. The post-resume ready + pid_discovered pair is the shape claudecode, codex and kiro-cli recordings all show after a process_exited — the row is revived on the same session_id rather than a new one being minted. The windows are generous (60 s) because copilot flushes NOTHING to events.jsonl on resume: the revival may not be observable until turn 2's user.message lands, in which case ready and working arrive back-to-back (as gemini-cli's recording shows). PROVISIONAL: the append-to-the-same-events.jsonl behaviour is evidenced by app.js (the resume path emits onto the same session object, targeting join(sessionStatePath,"events.jsonl"), carrying that file's byte size) and by the resumed process taking the original directory's lock, but no appended line was observed live because copilot's writer flushes nothing until a turn runs. model is NOT pinned: --model accepts only auto and the router resolves gpt-5-mini or claude-haiku-4.5 at runtime.
